title: Protocol for Imaging of Mitoflashes in Live Cardiomyocytes
protocol: Place a diameter 25 mm circular coverslip into a well using fine-tip forceps.
Coat the coverslips with 100 μL of 40 μg/mL laminin, spreading it evenly over the coverslip using a pipette tip.
Gently place the plate with coated coverslip into a 37°C incubator for at least 1 h but no more than 3 h.
Transfer freshly isolated cardiomyocytes to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 30 × g for 30 seconds.
Discard the supernatant using a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 4–8 mL of pre-warmed M199 culture medium.
Count cardiomyocytes using a traditional Hemocytometer.
Dilute the cells to a concentration of 2.5 × 10^5/mL with M199 culture medium.
Discard laminin from the coated plate without letting the coverslip dry.
Add 200 μL of cardiomyocyte suspension at a density of 2.5 × 10^5 cells to the center of the coated coverslip.
Place the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Wait for at least 2 hours to allow cardiomyocytes to attach to the coverslip.
Infect Adeno-mt-cpYFP Timing: 2 days
Express mitoflash biomarker, mt-cpYFP, in the mitochondrial matrix of cardiomyocytes.
Thaw an aliquoted Ad-mt-cpYFP virus on ice from -80°C.
Gently discard the 200 μl medium and add 1 ml fresh M199 culture medium.
Add proper Ad-mt-cpYFP (50 MOI) into the medium.
Gently move plates backward and forward, then right to left to right, repeat 2-3 times.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 1-2 hours.
Add 1 mL medium containing virus to enhance virus concentration and improve infection efficiency.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 48 hours to allow expression of cpYFP.
Monitor and take two-dimensional images of mitoflashes in adult cardiomyocytes.
Pre-warm KHB buffer to room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Thaw TMRM working solution and add 2 μL per well (1:1,000) for staining mitochondrial membrane potential at 37°C for 20-30 minutes.
Set the imaging parameters of Zen software for dual excitation images of mt-cpYFP.
Excite sequentially at 488 nm and then at 543 nm.
Collect emission at 505–545 nm after 488 nm excitation.
Collect emission at >560 nm after 543 nm excitation.
Acquire time-lapse x,y images at a resolution of 1,024 × 1,024 for 100 frames.
Set the sampling rate to 1 s per frame.
Completely turn on the 488 nm laser.
Allow the 543 nm laser to warm up for 3–5 minutes.
Remove the magnetic top of the Quick-Release Magnetic chamber.
Apply high vacuum grease evenly around the inside pedestal of the magnetic bottom.
Place the coverslip into the magnetic bottom.
Replace the magnetic top and add 1 ml KHB buffer.
Place the coverslip into the magnetic bottom of the imaging chamber.
Put the magnetic top back onto the chamber.
Hold the edge of the coverslip with forceps.
Add 1 mL KHB buffer into the chamber using a pipette.
Check for leakage by placing the imaging chamber on a Kimwipe.
Add one drop of oil on top of the 63× objective.
Place the chamber on the microscope stage above the objective, roughly in the center of the field of view.
Find and focus the cell sample in the eyepieces.
Move the cell sample to the center field of vision.
Choose only the 488 channel for imaging parameters setup (Gain: 450–600; Pinhole: 30–200; laser <10%).
Click on “Live” on the top left corner.
Adjust the focal position by rotating the knob until the mitochondria are focused.
Adjust the laser power, pinhole, gain, and digital offset.
Set the scan mode to frame in the imaging system.
Adjust the speed setting to 9.
Averaging set to number, 1.
Gain set between 450–600.
Pinhole size set from 30–200.
Laser power adjusted below 10% to prevent cell damage during long-time two-dimensional scanning.
Select a rod cardiomyocyte with clear mitochondrial pattern for imaging.
Acquire and save a 2D image of the selected cardiomyocyte with 100 frames using the imaging system.
Count the number of mitoflashes in the acquired images by eye while playing the 2D images using Zeiss LSM viewer software.
Analyze mitoflash timing from 5 to 30 minutes.
